title: Capacity for movement is an organisational principle in object representations: EEG data from Experiment 1
description: EEG dataset from Experiment 1 of a study on whether capacity for movement is an organisational principle in visual object representations. Twenty-four participants viewed images of moving or non-moving, natural or artificial objects, completing a time-pressured aliveness classification task and a passive RSVP viewing task with a fixation-colour detection response. The release includes raw BrainVision EEG, preprocessed EEGLAB and CoSMoMVPA data, decoding results, analysis code, and 400 CC0 stimulus images.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with BrainVision while participants classified single images as alive or not alive (1 s timeout) and, in a passive viewing task, watched rapid serial visual presentation streams while pressing a button when the fixation cross changed colour. Analyses included decoding, representational similarity analysis and GLMs.
